/-!
# The Birkhoff conjecture

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, George David Birkhoff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_David_Birkhoff)
- [Wikipedia, list of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
-/

namespace Birkhoff

open Set
open scoped RealInnerProductSpace

abbrev Plane := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)

/-- The signed area of the parallelogram spanned by two vectors in the Euclidean plane. -/
def cross (u v : Plane) : ℝ := u 0 * v 1 - u 1 * v 0

/-- The line through `x` and `y` is a supporting tangent line of the convex set `C`. -/
def IsTangentLine (C : Set Plane) (x y : Plane) : Prop :=
  x ≠ y ∧
    (∃ z ∈ C, ∃ t : ℝ, z = x + t • (y - x)) ∧
    ((∀ z ∈ C, 0 ≤ cross (y - x) (z - x)) ∨
      (∀ z ∈ C, cross (y - x) (z - x) ≤ 0))

/-- The unit vector pointing from `x` to `y` (and zero when the points coincide). -/
noncomputable def unitDirection (x y : Plane) : Plane := ‖y - x‖⁻¹ • (y - x)

/-- Three boundary points obey the Euclidean specular-reflection law at the middle point. -/
def IsBilliardReflection (f : Plane → ℝ) (x y z : Plane) : Prop :=
  f x = 0 ∧ f y = 0 ∧ f z = 0 ∧ x ≠ y ∧ y ≠ z ∧
    ∃ n : Plane, n ≠ 0 ∧
      (∀ v : Plane, fderiv ℝ f y v = inner ℝ n v) ∧
      unitDirection y z = unitDirection x y -
        (2 * inner ℝ (unitDirection x y) n / inner ℝ n n) • n

/-- A compact strictly convex set whose tangent trajectories are preserved by billiard reflection. -/
def IsConvexCaustic (f : Plane → ℝ) (K C : Set Plane) : Prop :=
  IsCompact C ∧ C.Nonempty ∧ (interior C).Nonempty ∧ StrictConvex ℝ C ∧
    C ⊆ interior K ∧
    ∀ ⦃x y z : Plane⦄, IsBilliardReflection f x y z →
      (IsTangentLine C x y ↔ IsTangentLine C y z)

/-- A smooth strictly convex billiard table, presented by a regular defining function.
Positive tangential Hessian means that its boundary has strictly positive curvature. -/
def IsSmoothStrictlyConvexTable (f : Plane → ℝ) (K : Set Plane) : Prop :=
  IsCompact K ∧ (interior K).Nonempty ∧ Convex ℝ K ∧
    K = {x | f x ≤ 0} ∧ ContDiff ℝ 2 f ∧
    ∀ x, f x = 0 →
      fderiv ℝ f x ≠ 0 ∧
        ∀ v : Plane, v ≠ 0 → fderiv ℝ f x v = 0 →
          0 < fderiv ℝ (fun y ↦ fderiv ℝ f y) x v v

/-- Local integrability: an inner collar of the boundary is foliated by a nested family of
convex caustics invariant under the billiard reflection law. -/
def IsLocallyIntegrable (f : Plane → ℝ) (K : Set Plane) : Prop :=
  ∃ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ ∧
    ∃ C : Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1 → Set Plane,
      (∀ t, IsConvexCaustic f K (C t)) ∧
      (∀ s t, s < t → C s ⊆ interior (C t)) ∧
      Pairwise (fun s t ↦ Disjoint (frontier (C s)) (frontier (C t))) ∧
      (⋃ t, frontier (C t)) =
        {x | x ∈ interior K ∧ Metric.infDist x (frontier K) < δ}

/-- A planar set is an ellipse if it is an affine image of the closed Euclidean unit disk. -/
def IsEllipse (K : Set Plane) : Prop :=
  ∃ c : Plane, ∃ L : Plane ≃L[ℝ] Plane, K = {x | ‖L (x - c)‖ ≤ 1}

/--
The Birkhoff conjecture asks whether every smooth strictly convex planar billiard table that is
integrable in a neighbourhood of its boundary has elliptic boundary (with circles included as
ellipses). Here local integrability means that an inner collar of the boundary is foliated by
nested convex caustics invariant under the billiard reflection map.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 37]
theorem birkhoff :
    answer(sorry) ↔
      ∀ (f : Plane → ℝ) (K : Set Plane),
        IsSmoothStrictlyConvexTable f K → IsLocallyIntegrable f K → IsEllipse K := by
  sorry

end Birkhoff
modeling_decisions: Interpreted the yes/no question using `answer(sorry) ↔ P`, where `P` is the conjectured positive classification of every qualifying table.

Modeled the billiard table as a compact convex subset of `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)` with nonempty interior, presented as the sublevel set of a globally `C²` defining function. Required a nonzero differential and positive second derivative in every nonzero tangent direction at the zero level, expressing a smooth boundary of strictly positive curvature.

Used the standard local meaning of integrability specified by the decomposition: an inner neighborhood (collar) of the table boundary is foliated by a nested one-parameter family of convex caustic curves. Did not require a foliation of the whole phase space.

Represented each convex caustic curve as the frontier of a compact strictly convex body with nonempty interior inside the table. The family is nested, has pairwise-disjoint frontiers, and its frontiers have union exactly equal to the collar.

Defined caustic invariance geometrically: a line supporting the caustic before a Euclidean specular reflection is a supporting line afterward, and conversely. This is the convex-caustic formulation of invariant curves for the billiard map.

Modeled an ellipse as the inverse image of the closed Euclidean unit disk under an invertible linear map after translation, equivalently an affine image of the disk. Thus the theorem classifies the filled table; because the table is compact and convex with nonempty interior, this is equivalent to saying its boundary is an ellipse. Circles are included.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Birkhoff conjecture (integrable billiards)

The *Birkhoff conjecture* asks: if a billiard table is strictly convex and integrable, is its
boundary necessarily an ellipse?

A *billiard table* is a planar domain bounded by a smooth closed curve. A point particle moves
inside it along straight lines and is reflected elastically at the boundary (angle of incidence
equals angle of reflection). The table is *strictly convex* if its boundary has strictly positive
curvature. The *billiard map* acts on the phase space of pairs `(p, v)` where `p` is a boundary
point and `v` is a unit velocity pointing strictly inward. The phase space is an open annulus
whose two boundary circles consist of the tangent directions `v = ± γ' / ‖γ'‖`.

Following the standard modern formulation (see Kaloshin–Sorrentino), the billiard is
*integrable* if a neighbourhood of the boundary of the phase space is foliated by closed
invariant curves. Each such curve winds once around the annulus and is a graph over the
boundary of the table; equivalently, a neighbourhood of the boundary of the table is foliated by
convex caustics. Ellipses (including circles) are integrable, and the conjecture is that they are
the only strictly convex integrable tables.

Bialy proved that if the *whole* phase space is foliated by invariant curves that are not
null-homotopic, then the table is a circle. Avila, De Simoi and Kaloshin, and Kaloshin and
Sorrentino proved local versions of the conjecture for perturbations of ellipses. The conjecture
itself is open.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia: George David Birkhoff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_David_Birkhoff)
- [Wikipedia: List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Wikipedia: Dynamical billiards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dynamical_billiards)
- V. Kaloshin, A. Sorrentino, *On the integrability of Birkhoff billiards*,
  Phil. Trans. R. Soc. A 376 (2018), [arXiv:1706.07030](https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.07030)
- V. Kaloshin, A. Sorrentino, *On the local Birkhoff conjecture for convex billiards*,
  Ann. of Math. 188 (2018), [arXiv:1612.09194](https://arxiv.org/abs/1612.09194)
- A. Avila, J. De Simoi, V. Kaloshin, *An integrable deformation of an ellipse of small
  eccentricity is an ellipse*, Ann. of Math. 184 (2016),
  [arXiv:1412.2853](https://arxiv.org/abs/1412.2853)
- M. Bialy, *Convex billiards and a theorem by E. Hopf*, Math. Z. 214 (1993), 147–154
-/

open scoped EuclideanGeometry
open Real Topology

namespace Birkhoff

/-- The signed area (determinant) of two vectors `a b : ℝ²`. It is positive iff `b` points
strictly to the left of `a`. -/
def signedArea (a b : ℝ²) : ℝ := a 0 * b 1 - a 1 * b 0

@[category API, AMS 51]
lemma signedArea_swap (a b : ℝ²) : signedArea b a = -signedArea a b := by
  simp only [signedArea]
  ring

/-- A parametrised curve `γ : ℝ → ℝ²` is the boundary of a *strictly convex billiard table* if it
is a `C²`, `1`-periodic, simple closed curve whose signed curvature is everywhere strictly
positive. Positivity of `signedArea (γ' t) (γ'' t)` forces `γ' t ≠ 0` (so `γ` is regular),
fixes the counterclockwise orientation (the table lies to the left of `γ'`), and is equivalent to
strictly positive curvature. -/
structure IsStrictlyConvexTable (γ : ℝ → ℝ²) : Prop where
  contDiff : ContDiff ℝ 2 γ
  periodic : Function.Periodic γ 1
  injOn : Set.InjOn γ (Set.Ico 0 1)
  curvature_pos : ∀ t, 0 < signedArea (deriv γ t) (deriv (deriv γ) t)

/-- The (open) phase space of the billiard in the table with boundary `γ`: pairs `(p, v)` where
`p = γ t` is a boundary point and `v` is a unit vector pointing strictly into the table, i.e.
strictly to the left of the tangent vector `γ' t`. -/
def phaseSpace (γ : ℝ → ℝ²) : Set (ℝ² × ℝ²) :=
  {x | ∃ t, x.1 = γ t ∧ ‖x.2‖ = 1 ∧ 0 < signedArea (deriv γ t) x.2}

/-- The boundary of the phase space: pairs `(p, v)` where `p = γ t` is a boundary point and `v`
is a unit vector tangent to the boundary, i.e. `v = ± γ' t / ‖γ' t‖`. It consists of the two
boundary circles of the phase space annulus. -/
def phaseSpaceBoundary (γ : ℝ → ℝ²) : Set (ℝ² × ℝ²) :=
  {x | ∃ t, x.1 = γ t ∧ ‖x.2‖ = 1 ∧ signedArea (deriv γ t) x.2 = 0}

/-- One step of the billiard dynamics: from `x = (p, v)`, the particle travels along the ray
`p + l • v` (`l > 0`) until it hits the boundary again at `q = γ t`, where its velocity `v` is
reflected across the tangent line `ℝ ∙ γ' t`. For a strictly convex table the ray from a
boundary point in a strictly inward direction meets the boundary in exactly one further point,
so `y` is uniquely determined by `x`: `BilliardStep γ x y` is the graph of the billiard map. -/
def BilliardStep (γ : ℝ → ℝ²) (x y : ℝ² × ℝ²) : Prop :=
  x ∈ phaseSpace γ ∧ y ∈ phaseSpace γ ∧ (∃ l : ℝ, 0 < l ∧ y.1 = x.1 + l • x.2) ∧
    ∃ t, y.1 = γ t ∧ y.2 = (ℝ ∙ deriv γ t).reflection x.2

/-- A set `L` in the phase space is an *invariant curve* of the billiard in the table with
boundary `γ` if it is a compact set which is a graph over the boundary of the table (over each
boundary point lies exactly one point of `L`), and it is invariant under the billiard map and its
inverse. Compactness of the graph makes `L` a continuous closed curve winding once around the
phase space annulus. By Birkhoff's theorem, every closed invariant curve of the billiard map which
is not null-homotopic is such a graph. -/
structure IsInvariantCurve (γ : ℝ → ℝ²) (L : Set (ℝ² × ℝ²)) : Prop where
  subset : L ⊆ phaseSpace γ
  isCompact : IsCompact L
  existsUnique : ∀ p ∈ Set.range γ, ∃! v, (p, v) ∈ L
  invariant : ∀ x y, BilliardStep γ x y → (x ∈ L ↔ y ∈ L)

/-- The billiard in the table with boundary `γ` is *integrable* if a neighbourhood of the boundary
of the phase space is foliated by invariant curves: there is a family `𝓛` of pairwise disjoint
invariant curves whose union contains every point of the phase space sufficiently close to any
given point of the boundary of the phase space (i.e. to any tangent direction). -/
def IsIntegrable (γ : ℝ → ℝ²) : Prop :=
  ∃ 𝓛 : Set (Set (ℝ² × ℝ²)), (∀ L ∈ 𝓛, IsInvariantCurve γ L) ∧ 𝓛.PairwiseDisjoint id ∧
    ∀ b ∈ phaseSpaceBoundary γ, ∀ᶠ x in 𝓝[phaseSpace γ] b, x ∈ ⋃₀ 𝓛

/-- A subset of the plane is an *ellipse* if it is the locus of points whose distances to two
foci `f₁ f₂` sum to a constant `2a` with `2a > dist f₁ f₂`. Circles are the case `f₁ = f₂`. -/
def IsEllipse (C : Set ℝ²) : Prop :=
  ∃ (f₁ f₂ : ℝ²) (a : ℝ), dist f₁ f₂ < 2 * a ∧ C = {p | dist p f₁ + dist p f₂ = 2 * a}

/--
**Birkhoff conjecture.**
If a billiard table is strictly convex and integrable, is its boundary necessarily an ellipse?

Here a strictly convex table is bounded by a `C²` simple closed curve `γ` of strictly positive
curvature, the billiard is integrable if a neighbourhood of the boundary of its phase space is
foliated by closed invariant curves, and an ellipse may be a circle. The conjectured answer is
yes.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 37 51]
theorem birkhoff :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ γ : ℝ → ℝ², IsStrictlyConvexTable γ → IsIntegrable γ →
      IsEllipse (Set.range γ) := by
  sorry

/- Sanity checks: the unit circle is a strictly convex table and an ellipse. -/

/-- The unit circle is an ellipse. -/
@[category test, AMS 51]
theorem isEllipse_sphere : IsEllipse (Metric.sphere (0 : ℝ²) 1) := by
  refine ⟨0, 0, 1, by simp, ?_⟩
  ext p
  simp only [Metric.mem_sphere, Set.mem_setOf_eq]
  constructor <;> intro h <;> linarith

/-- The unit circle, traversed once counterclockwise with period `1`. -/
noncomputable def unitCircle (t : ℝ) : ℝ² := !₂[cos (2 * π * t), sin (2 * π * t)]

@[category API, AMS 53]
lemma hasDerivAt_unitCircle (t : ℝ) :
    HasDerivAt unitCircle !₂[-(2 * π * sin (2 * π * t)), 2 * π * cos (2 * π * t)] t := by
  have h1 : HasDerivAt (fun t => cos (2 * π * t)) (-(2 * π * sin (2 * π * t))) t := by
    have := (hasDerivAt_cos (2 * π * t)).comp t ((hasDerivAt_id t).const_mul (2 * π))
    simpa [Function.comp_def, mul_comm] using this
  have h2 : HasDerivAt (fun t => sin (2 * π * t)) (2 * π * cos (2 * π * t)) t := by
    have := (hasDerivAt_sin (2 * π * t)).comp t ((hasDerivAt_id t).const_mul (2 * π))
    simpa [Function.comp_def, mul_comm] using this
  have hpi : HasDerivAt (fun t => ![cos (2 * π * t), sin (2 * π * t)])
      ![-(2 * π * sin (2 * π * t)), 2 * π * cos (2 * π * t)] t := by
    rw [hasDerivAt_pi]
    intro i
    fin_cases i
    · simpa using h1
    · simpa using h2
  exact (PiLp.hasFDerivAt_toLp 2 _).comp_hasDerivAt t hpi

@[category API, AMS 53]
lemma deriv_unitCircle :
    deriv unitCircle = fun t => !₂[-(2 * π * sin (2 * π * t)), 2 * π * cos (2 * π * t)] :=
  funext fun t => (hasDerivAt_unitCircle t).deriv

@[category API, AMS 53]
lemma hasDerivAt_deriv_unitCircle (t : ℝ) :
    HasDerivAt (deriv unitCircle)
      !₂[-(2 * π * (2 * π * cos (2 * π * t))), -(2 * π * (2 * π * sin (2 * π * t)))] t := by
  rw [deriv_unitCircle]
  have h1 : HasDerivAt (fun t => -(2 * π * sin (2 * π * t)))
      (-(2 * π * (2 * π * cos (2 * π * t)))) t := by
    have := (hasDerivAt_sin (2 * π * t)).comp t ((hasDerivAt_id t).const_mul (2 * π))
    have := (this.const_mul (2 * π)).neg
    simpa [Function.comp_def, mul_comm, mul_left_comm, mul_assoc] using this
  have h2 : HasDerivAt (fun t => 2 * π * cos (2 * π * t))
      (-(2 * π * (2 * π * sin (2 * π * t)))) t := by
    have := (hasDerivAt_cos (2 * π * t)).comp t ((hasDerivAt_id t).const_mul (2 * π))
    have := this.const_mul (2 * π)
    simpa [Function.comp_def, mul_comm, mul_left_comm, mul_assoc] using this
  have hpi : HasDerivAt (fun t => ![-(2 * π * sin (2 * π * t)), 2 * π * cos (2 * π * t)])
      ![-(2 * π * (2 * π * cos (2 * π * t))), -(2 * π * (2 * π * sin (2 * π * t)))] t := by
    rw [hasDerivAt_pi]
    intro i
    fin_cases i
    · simpa using h1
    · simpa using h2
  exact (PiLp.hasFDerivAt_toLp 2 _).comp_hasDerivAt t hpi

/-- The unit circle is a strictly convex billiard table. -/
@[category test, AMS 53]
theorem isStrictlyConvexTable_unitCircle : IsStrictlyConvexTable unitCircle where
  contDiff := by
    unfold unitCircle
    refine PiLp.contDiff_toLp.comp ?_
    rw [contDiff_pi]
    intro i
    fin_cases i
    · exact Real.contDiff_cos.comp (contDiff_const.mul contDiff_id)
    · exact Real.contDiff_sin.comp (contDiff_const.mul contDiff_id)
  periodic := by
    intro t
    simp only [unitCircle, mul_add, mul_one]
    rw [cos_add_two_pi, sin_add_two_pi]
  injOn := by
    intro s hs t ht hst
    simp only [unitCircle] at hst
    have hc : cos (2 * π * s) = cos (2 * π * t) := by
      have := congrArg (fun v : ℝ² => v 0) hst
      simpa using this
    have hsn : sin (2 * π * s) = sin (2 * π * t) := by
      have := congrArg (fun v : ℝ² => v 1) hst
      simpa using this
    have h1 : cos (2 * π * t - 2 * π * s) = 1 := by
      rw [cos_sub, ← hc, ← hsn]
      linear_combination cos_sq_add_sin_sq (2 * π * s)
    obtain ⟨hs0, hs1⟩ := hs
    obtain ⟨ht0, ht1⟩ := ht
    have := (cos_eq_one_iff_of_lt_of_lt (by nlinarith [pi_pos]) (by nlinarith [pi_pos])).mp h1
    nlinarith [pi_pos]
  curvature_pos := by
    intro t
    rw [(hasDerivAt_deriv_unitCircle t).deriv, deriv_unitCircle]
    simp only [signedArea]
    simp
    have : 2 * π * sin (2 * π * t) * (2 * π * (2 * π * sin (2 * π * t))) +
        2 * π * cos (2 * π * t) * (2 * π * (2 * π * cos (2 * π * t))) =
        8 * π ^ 3 * (sin (2 * π * t) ^ 2 + cos (2 * π * t) ^ 2) := by ring
    rw [this, sin_sq_add_cos_sq]
    positivity

@[category API, AMS 53]
lemma unitCircle_zero : unitCircle 0 = !₂[1, 0] := by
  simp [unitCircle]

@[category API, AMS 53]
lemma unitCircle_half : unitCircle (1 / 2) = !₂[-1, 0] := by
  simp only [unitCircle, show 2 * π * (1 / 2) = π by ring]
  simp

@[category API, AMS 53]
lemma deriv_unitCircle_zero : deriv unitCircle 0 = !₂[0, 2 * π] := by
  rw [deriv_unitCircle]
  simp

@[category API, AMS 53]
lemma deriv_unitCircle_half : deriv unitCircle (1 / 2) = !₂[0, -(2 * π)] := by
  rw [deriv_unitCircle]
  simp only [show 2 * π * (1 / 2) = π by ring]
  simp

/-- In the unit circle, the particle starting at `(1, 0)` with velocity `(-1, 0)` travels along
the diameter, hits the boundary at `(-1, 0)` and bounces back with velocity `(1, 0)`. -/
@[category test, AMS 37]
theorem billiardStep_unitCircle_diameter :
    BilliardStep unitCircle (!₂[1, 0], !₂[-1, 0]) (!₂[-1, 0], !₂[1, 0]) := by
  have hn₁ : ‖(!₂[-1, 0] : ℝ²)‖ = 1 := by simp [EuclideanSpace.norm_eq, Fin.sum_univ_two]
  have hn₂ : ‖(!₂[1, 0] : ℝ²)‖ = 1 := by simp [EuclideanSpace.norm_eq, Fin.sum_univ_two]
  refine ⟨⟨0, unitCircle_zero.symm, hn₁, ?_⟩, ⟨1 / 2, unitCircle_half.symm, hn₂, ?_⟩,
    ⟨2, by norm_num, ?_⟩, ⟨1 / 2, unitCircle_half.symm, ?_⟩⟩
  · rw [deriv_unitCircle_zero]
    simp [signedArea]

/-!
# Birkhoff conjecture

The *Birkhoff conjecture* (also called the *Birkhoff–Poritsky conjecture*) asks whether a
strictly convex planar billiard table whose billiard dynamics is integrable must be bounded by
an ellipse.

A billiard table is a strictly convex domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ with $C^2$ boundary of
strictly positive curvature. A point mass moves inside $\Omega$ along straight lines and is
reflected elastically at the boundary: the angle of reflection equals the angle of incidence.
The billiard map acts on the phase cylinder $\partial\Omega \times (0, \pi)$ of pairs
(boundary point, angle between the outgoing direction and the tangent). Following Kaloshin and
Sorrentino, the billiard is *integrable* if a neighbourhood of the boundary
$\partial\Omega \times \{0, \pi\}$ of the phase cylinder is foliated by continuous invariant
curves. Equivalently, a neighbourhood of $\partial\Omega$ inside $\Omega$ is foliated by convex
caustics. The whole-phase-space version of the question is Bialy's theorem: then $\Omega$ is a disc.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, George David Birkhoff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_David_Birkhoff)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics]
  (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Wikipedia, Dynamical billiards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dynamical_billiards)
- [KS18] Kaloshin, V., Sorrentino, A. _On the local Birkhoff conjecture for convex billiards_.
  Annals of Mathematics 188 (2018), 315–380. [arXiv:1612.09194](https://arxiv.org/abs/1612.09194)
- [BM22] Bialy, M., Mironov, A. E. _The Birkhoff-Poritsky conjecture for centrally-symmetric
  $C^2$-smooth convex planar billiards_. Annals of Mathematics 196 (2022), 389–413.
  [arXiv:2008.03566](https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.03566)
- [Bi93] Bialy, M. _Convex billiards and a theorem by E. Hopf_. Math. Z. 214 (1993), 147–154.
-/

open Set Real EuclideanGeometry

namespace Birkhoff

/--
A map `γ : ℝ → ℝ²` is a *strictly convex curve* if it is a `1`-periodic `C²` parametrisation of a
simple closed curve with strictly positive curvature, i.e. `γ' × γ'' > 0` everywhere. Positivity
of `γ' × γ''` forces `γ' ≠ 0`, so `γ` is regular, and the orientation is counterclockwise, so the
enclosed domain lies to the left of `γ`. The image of such a curve is the boundary of a strictly
convex billiard table.
-/
structure IsStrictlyConvexCurve (γ : ℝ → ℝ²) : Prop where
  periodic : Function.Periodic γ 1
  contDiff : ContDiff ℝ 2 γ
  injOn : InjOn γ (Ico 0 1)
  curvature_pos : ∀ t, 0 < o.areaForm (deriv γ t) (deriv (deriv γ) t)

/--
The direction of the billiard trajectory leaving the boundary point `γ s` at angle `θ`, measured
counterclockwise from the tangent vector `deriv γ s`. For `θ ∈ (0, π)` it points into the table.
-/
noncomputable def direction (γ : ℝ → ℝ²) (s θ : ℝ) : ℝ² :=
  o.rotation θ (deriv γ s)

/--
The graph of the billiard map of the table bounded by `γ`. `BilliardRel γ (s, θ) (s', θ')` holds
when `θ, θ' ∈ (0, π)`, the trajectory leaving `γ s` at angle `θ` next hits the boundary at `γ s'`,
and after elastic reflection in the tangent line at `γ s'` (the angle of reflection equals the
angle of incidence) it leaves `γ s'` at angle `θ'`.
-/
def BilliardRel (γ : ℝ → ℝ²) (x y : ℝ × ℝ) : Prop :=
  x.2 ∈ Ioo 0 π ∧ y.2 ∈ Ioo 0 π ∧
    (∃ r > 0, γ y.1 = γ x.1 + r • direction γ x.1 x.2) ∧
    ∃ c > 0, direction γ y.1 y.2 = c • (ℝ ∙ deriv γ y.1).reflection (direction γ x.1 x.2)

/--
An *invariant curve* of the billiard in the table bounded by `γ` is a continuous closed curve
winding once around the phase cylinder `∂Ω × (0, π)` that the billiard map sends to itself.
We represent it as the graph `{(s, f s)}` of a continuous `1`-periodic function `f : ℝ → (0, π)`.
By Birkhoff's theorem on twist maps, every homotopically non-trivial invariant curve of the
billiard map is such a graph.
-/
def IsInvariantCurve (γ : ℝ → ℝ²) (C : Set (ℝ × ℝ)) : Prop :=
  (∃ f : ℝ → ℝ, Continuous f ∧ Function.Periodic f 1 ∧ (∀ s, f s ∈ Ioo 0 π) ∧
    C = {x | x.2 = f x.1}) ∧
  ∀ x y, BilliardRel γ x y → (x ∈ C ↔ y ∈ C)

/--
The billiard in the table bounded by `γ` is *integrable* if a neighbourhood of the boundary
`∂Ω × {0, π}` of the phase cylinder `∂Ω × (0, π)` is foliated by invariant curves: for some
`ε > 0`, the strips `0 < θ < ε` and `π - ε < θ < π` are covered by pairwise disjoint invariant
curves.
-/
def IsIntegrableBilliard (γ : ℝ → ℝ²) : Prop :=
  ∃ ε > 0, ∃ F : Set (Set (ℝ × ℝ)), (∀ C ∈ F, IsInvariantCurve γ C) ∧ F.PairwiseDisjoint id ∧
    {x : ℝ × ℝ | x.2 ∈ Ioo 0 ε ∪ Ioo (π - ε) π} ⊆ ⋃₀ F

bijection of the plane. Circles are ellipses. -/
def IsEllipse (E : Set ℝ²) : Prop :=
  ∃ f : ℝ² ≃ᵃ[ℝ] ℝ², E = f '' Metric.sphere 0 1

/-- The unit circle is an ellipse. -/
@[category test, AMS 51]
theorem isEllipse_sphere : IsEllipse (Metric.sphere 0 1) :=
  ⟨AffineEquiv.refl ℝ ℝ², by simp⟩

Here a strictly convex table is bounded by a `C²` simple closed curve `γ` of strictly positive
curvature, and integrable means that a neighbourhood of the boundary of the phase cylinder of the
billiard map is foliated by continuous invariant curves. The conjectured answer is yes.
-/

    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ γ : ℝ → ℝ², IsStrictlyConvexCurve γ → IsIntegrableBilliard γ →
      IsEllipse (range γ) := by
  sorry

end Birkhoff

`direction γ s' θ'` in which it leaves `γ s'` is the mirror image of its incoming direction in

graph of the billiard map.

def BilliardRel (γ : ℝ → ℝ²) (p q : ℝ × ℝ) : Prop :=
  p.2 ∈ Set.Ioo 0 π ∧ q.2 ∈ Set.Ioo 0 π ∧
    (∃ r > 0, γ q.1 = γ p.1 + r • direction γ p.1 p.2) ∧
    direction γ q.1 q.2 = (ℝ ∙ unitTangent γ q.1).reflection (direction γ p.1 p.2)

written as the graph of a continuous function `f` from the boundary (parametrised with period `1`)
to the angles `(0, π)`. Invariance means that the billiard map sends the graph of `f` onto itself.

structure IsInvariantCurve (γ : ℝ → ℝ²) (f : ℝ → ℝ) : Prop where
  continuous : Continuous f
  periodic : Function.Periodic f 1
  mem_Ioo : ∀ s, f s ∈ Set.Ioo 0 π
  forward_invariant : ∀ s q, BilliardRel γ (s, f s) q → q.2 = f q.1
  backward_invariant : ∀ p s, BilliardRel γ p (s, f s) → p.2 = f p.1

  ∃ F : Set (ℝ → ℝ), (∀ f ∈ F, IsInvariantCurve γ f) ∧

automorphism of the plane. Circles are ellipses. -/

# Birkhoff conjecture

If a billiard table is strictly convex and integrable, is its boundary necessarily an ellipse?

A *billiard table* is a bounded strictly convex planar domain $\Omega$ whose boundary
$\partial\Omega$ is a $C^2$ closed curve with strictly positive curvature. The billiard map
sends an oriented chord of $\Omega$ to the chord obtained by reflecting it, at its endpoint, across
the tangent line to $\partial\Omega$ (angle of incidence equals angle of reflection). The phase
space of oriented chords is an open cylinder, whose boundary $\{\theta = 0\}$ consists of the
degenerate chords tangent to $\partial\Omega$. The billiard is *integrable* if a neighbourhood of
$\{\theta = 0\}$ in the phase cylinder is foliated by homotopically nontrivial invariant curves
(equivalently, a neighbourhood of $\partial\Omega$ inside $\Omega$ is foliated by convex caustics).
If the whole phase cylinder is foliated by such curves the table is a disc by a theorem of Bialy,
so the conjecture is about integrability near the boundary.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Wikipedia, George David Birkhoff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_David_Birkhoff)
- [V. Kaloshin, A. Sorrentino, *On the integrability of Birkhoff billiards*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.04030)
- [V. Kaloshin, A. Sorrentino, *On the local Birkhoff conjecture for convex billiards*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1612.09194)
- [A. Avila, J. De Simoi, V. Kaloshin, *An integrable deformation of an ellipse of small eccentricity is an ellipse*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1412.2853)
- M. Bialy, *Convex billiards and a theorem by E. Hopf*, Math. Z. 214 (1993), 147–154.
-/

open scoped EuclideanGeometry

namespace Birkhoff

/-- `IsStrictlyConvexCurve γ` says that `γ : ℝ → ℝ²` is a $C^2$ simple closed curve of period `1`,
positively oriented, with strictly positive curvature. The last condition is
$\det(\gamma'(t), \gamma''(t)) > 0$ for all $t$; it forces $\gamma'(t) \neq 0$, so `γ` is regular
and its signed curvature $\det(\gamma', \gamma'') / \|\gamma'\|^3$ is strictly positive. Such a
curve bounds a strictly convex billiard table. -/
structure IsStrictlyConvexCurve (γ : ℝ → ℝ²) : Prop where
  periodic : Function.Periodic γ 1
  contDiff : ContDiff ℝ 2 γ
  injOn : Set.InjOn γ (Set.Ico 0 1)
  curvature_pos : ∀ t, 0 < positiveOrientation.areaForm (deriv γ t) (deriv (deriv γ) t)

/-- `IsBilliardStep γ s₀ s₁ s₂` is the law of reflection at `γ s₁`: the chord from `γ s₀` to `γ s₁`
is nondegenerate, and the chord from `γ s₁` to `γ s₂` points in the direction obtained by reflecting
the incoming direction `γ s₁ - γ s₀` across the tangent line to `γ` at `γ s₁`. For a strictly
convex curve this determines `s₂` modulo `1`, and `(s₀, s₁) ↦ (s₁, s₂)` is the billiard map on
the phase space of oriented chords. -/
def IsBilliardStep (γ : ℝ → ℝ²) (s₀ s₁ s₂ : ℝ) : Prop :=
  γ s₀ ≠ γ s₁ ∧ ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ γ s₂ - γ s₁ = c • (ℝ ∙ deriv γ s₁).reflection (γ s₁ - γ s₀)

/-- The curve in the phase space of oriented chords `(s₀, s₁)` (the chord from `γ s₀` to `γ s₁`)
determined by a function `δ`: it consists of the chords with `s₁ ≡ s₀ + δ s₀ (mod 1)`. When `δ` is
continuous, `1`-periodic and takes values in `(0, 1)`, this is the graph of a continuous function
on the position circle, i.e. a homotopically nontrivial closed curve in the phase cylinder. -/
def leaf (δ : ℝ → ℝ) : Set (ℝ × ℝ) :=
  {p | ∃ k : ℤ, p.2 = p.1 + δ p.1 + k}

/-- `IsInvariantCurve γ δ` says that `leaf δ` is a homotopically nontrivial closed curve in the
phase cylinder of the billiard in the table bounded by `γ`, which is invariant under the billiard
map: for every billiard step `(s₀, s₁) ↦ (s₁, s₂)`, the chord `(s₀, s₁)` lies on the curve if and
only if `(s₁, s₂)` does. -/
structure IsInvariantCurve (γ : ℝ → ℝ²) (δ : ℝ → ℝ) : Prop where
  continuous : Continuous δ
  periodic : Function.Periodic δ 1
  mem_Ioo : ∀ s, δ s ∈ Set.Ioo 0 1
  invariant : ∀ s₀ s₁ s₂, IsBilliardStep γ s₀ s₁ s₂ → ((s₀, s₁) ∈ leaf δ ↔ (s₁, s₂) ∈ leaf δ)

/-- `IsIntegrable γ` says that the billiard in the table bounded by `γ` is integrable (near the
boundary): there is a neighbourhood of the boundary `{θ = 0}` of the phase cylinder which is
foliated by homotopically nontrivial invariant curves. Concretely, there is a set `F` of invariant
curves whose leaves are pairwise disjoint and whose union is an open set containing all chords
`(s₀, s₁)` with `0 < s₁ - s₀ < ε` for some `ε > 0`. In the coordinates `(s₀, s₁)`, the chords with
`s₁ - s₀ → 0⁺` are exactly those approaching the boundary component `{θ = 0}`, where `θ` is the
angle between the chord and the (positively oriented) tangent line at `γ s₀`. -/
def IsIntegrable (γ : ℝ → ℝ²) : Prop :=
  ∃ (F : Set (ℝ → ℝ)) (ε : ℝ), 0 < ε ∧ (∀ δ ∈ F, IsInvariantCurve γ δ) ∧
    F.PairwiseDisjoint leaf ∧ IsOpen (⋃ δ ∈ F, leaf δ) ∧
    {p : ℝ × ℝ | 0 < p.2 - p.1 ∧ p.2 - p.1 < ε} ⊆ ⋃ δ ∈ F, leaf δ

/-- A subset of the plane is an ellipse if it is the image of the unit circle under an affine
automorphism of the plane. Circles are ellipses. -/
def IsEllipse (E : Set ℝ²) : Prop :=
  ∃ f : ℝ² ≃ᵃ[ℝ] ℝ², E = f '' Metric.sphere 0 1

  !₂[Real.cos (2 * Real.pi * t), Real.sin (2 * Real.pi * t)]

@[category test, AMS 53]
theorem isStrictlyConvexCurve_unitCircle : IsStrictlyConvexCurve unitCircle := by
  sorry

theorem isIntegrable_unitCircle : IsIntegrable unitCircle := by
  sorry

-/

It is one-periodic, is injective modulo that period, is regular, and has strictly positive
curvature.
-/
def IsStrictlyConvexTable (γ : ℝ → Plane) : Prop :=
  ContDiff ℝ 2 γ ∧
    Function.Periodic γ 1 ∧
    (∀ s t, γ s = γ t ↔ ∃ k : ℤ, t = s + k) ∧
    (∀ s, deriv γ s ≠ 0) ∧
    ∀ s, 0 < det (deriv γ s) (deriv (deriv γ) s)

/--
The specular reflection law for three successive impacts `γ s`, `γ (s + a)`, and
`γ (s + a + b)`. Since both chord directions are normalized, equality of their tangential
components says that the incoming direction is reflected across the tangent line.
-/
def IsBilliardStep (γ : ℝ → Plane) (s a b : ℝ) : Prop :=
  inner ℝ ((‖γ (s + a) - γ s‖ : ℝ)⁻¹ • (γ (s + a) - γ s)) (deriv γ (s + a)) =
    inner ℝ ((‖γ (s + a + b) - γ (s + a)‖ : ℝ)⁻¹ •
      (γ (s + a + b) - γ (s + a))) (deriv γ (s + a))

/--
The billiard is integrable near the grazing boundary of its phase cylinder. For some
`0 < ε < 1`, the chord-coordinate collar `0 < a < ε` is continuously foliated by periodic

collar bijectively, and every graph is invariant under the billiard reflection law.
-/

  ∃ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε ∧ ε < 1 ∧
    ∃ leaves : ℝ → ℝ → ℝ,
      ContinuousOn (fun p : ℝ × ℝ ↦ leaves p.1 p.2) (Ioo 0 ε ×ˢ univ) ∧
      (∀ c ∈ Ioo 0 ε, Function.Periodic (leaves c) 1) ∧
      (∀ s, Set.BijOn (fun c ↦ leaves c s) (Ioo 0 ε) (Ioo 0 ε)) ∧
      ∀ c ∈ Ioo 0 ε, ∀ s,
        IsBilliardStep γ s (leaves c s) (leaves c (s + leaves c s))

def HasEllipticImage (γ : ℝ → Plane) : Prop :=
  ∃ center u v : Plane,
    LinearIndependent ℝ ![u, v] ∧
      range γ = range (fun θ : ℝ ↦ center + Real.cos θ • u + Real.sin θ • v)

The Birkhoff conjecture: if a planar billiard table has a smooth strictly convex boundary and a
neighborhood of the grazing boundary of its phase cylinder is foliated by invariant curves, then
its boundary is an ellipse (with circles included). Is the answer yes?
-/

theorem birkhoff : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ γ : ℝ → Plane,
    IsStrictlyConvexTable γ → IsIntegrable γ → HasEllipticImage γ := by
  sorry

end Birkhoff

namespace Birkhoff

open Set

/-- The Euclidean plane. -/
abbrev Plane := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)

/-- The determinant of two vectors in the oriented Euclidean plane. -/
def det (x y : Plane) : ℝ := x 0 * y 1 - x 1 * y 0

/-- A positively oriented, simple, $1$-periodic $C^2$ parametrization of a closed planar curve
with strictly positive curvature. -/
def IsStrictlyConvexBoundary (γ : ℝ → Plane) : Prop :=
  ContDiff ℝ 2 γ ∧
  (∀ s t, γ s = γ t ↔ ∃ n : ℤ, t = s + n) ∧
  ∀ s, 0 < det (deriv γ s) (deriv (deriv γ) s)

/-- Three lifted parameters describe successive impacts of the billiard map. The displayed
equality is the specular-reflection law: the unit incoming and outgoing directions have equal
tangential components. -/
def IsBilliardTransition (γ : ℝ → Plane) (s t u : ℝ) : Prop :=
  s < t ∧ t < u ∧ u < t + 1 ∧
    inner ℝ (‖γ t - γ s‖⁻¹ • (γ t - γ s)) (deriv γ t) =
      inner ℝ (‖γ u - γ t‖⁻¹ • (γ u - γ t)) (deriv γ t)

/-- The billiard is integrable near the grazing boundary of its phase cylinder: some collar
`0 < t - s < δ` is continuously foliated by periodic graph curves, and every leaf is invariant
under the billiard reflection relation. -/
def IsLocallyIntegrableBilliard (γ : ℝ → Plane) : Prop :=
  ∃ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ ∧ δ < 1 ∧ ∃ leaf : ℝ × ℝ → ℝ,
    Continuous leaf ∧
    (∀ r s, leaf (r, s + 1) = leaf (r, s) + 1) ∧
    (∀ s, Set.BijOn (fun r => leaf (r, s)) (Set.Ioo 0 1) (Set.Ioo s (s + δ))) ∧
    ∀ r ∈ Set.Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1, ∀ s,
      IsBilliardTransition γ s (leaf (r, s)) (leaf (r, leaf (r, s)))

/-- A planar curve is an ellipse if its image is a translate of the image of the unit circle
under an invertible linear map. This includes circles. -/
def HasEllipticImage (γ : ℝ → Plane) : Prop :=
  ∃ (c : Plane) (e : Plane ≃ₗ[ℝ] Plane),
    Set.range γ = (fun x => c + e x) '' Metric.sphere 0 1

/-- **Birkhoff conjecture.** Is the boundary of every strictly convex integrable planar billiard
table necessarily an ellipse (with circles included)? Here “integrable” means that a neighborhood
of the grazing boundary of the phase cylinder is foliated by invariant curves, rather than that
the entire phase cylinder is foliated. -/
@[category research open, AMS 37]
theorem birkhoff :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ γ : ℝ → Plane,
      IsStrictlyConvexBoundary γ → IsLocallyIntegrableBilliard γ → HasEllipticImage γ := by
  sorry

end Birkhoff

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, George David Birkhoff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_David_Birkhoff)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)

namespace Birkhoff

open Set

/-- A parametrized billiard boundary is strictly convex when it is a simple, closed, twice
continuously differentiable curve with everywhere positive signed curvature. The parameter has
been normalized to have period one. -/
def IsStrictlyConvexBoundary (γ : ℝ → ℂ) : Prop :=
  ContDiff ℝ 2 γ ∧
    Function.Periodic γ 1 ∧
    (∀ s t, γ s = γ t ↔ ∃ k : ℤ, t = s + (k : ℝ)) ∧
    ∀ s, 0 < ((starRingEnd ℂ (deriv γ s)) * deriv (deriv γ) s).im

/-- The unit chord from the boundary point with parameter `s` to the one with parameter `s + d`. -/
noncomputable def unitChord (γ : ℝ → ℂ) (s d : ℝ) : ℂ :=
  (γ (s + d) - γ s) / ‖γ (s + d) - γ s‖

/-- The billiard relation in phase coordinates `(s, d)`, in which `s` is the current boundary
parameter and `s + d` is the next impact. At that impact, equality of the tangential components
of the incoming and outgoing unit chords is the specular-reflection law. -/
def IsBilliardStep (γ : ℝ → ℂ) (x y : ℝ × ℝ) : Prop :=
  y.1 = x.1 + x.2 ∧
    ((starRingEnd ℂ (unitChord γ x.1 x.2)) * deriv γ y.1).re =
      ((starRingEnd ℂ (unitChord γ y.1 y.2)) * deriv γ y.1).re

/-- A billiard boundary is integrable near the grazing boundary of its phase cylinder if some
collar `0 < d < η` is continuously foliated by periodic invariant graphs `d = f a s`.
The unique parameter `a` labels the leaf through each phase point in the collar. -/
def IsIntegrableBilliard (γ : ℝ → ℂ) : Prop :=
  ∃ η : ℝ, 0 < η ∧ η < 1 ∧ ∃ f : ℝ → ℝ → ℝ,
    Continuous (fun p : ℝ × ℝ ↦ f p.1 p.2) ∧
    (∀ a ∈ Ioo 0 η, Function.Periodic (f a) 1) ∧
    (∀ a ∈ Ioo 0 η, ∀ s, f a s ∈ Ioo 0 η) ∧
    (∀ s d, d ∈ Ioo 0 η → ∃! a, a ∈ Ioo 0 η ∧ f a s = d) ∧
    ∀ a ∈ Ioo 0 η, ∀ s ε, ε ∈ Ioo 0 η →
      IsBilliardStep γ (s, f a s) (s + f a s, ε) ↔ ε = f a (s + f a s)

/-- A closed planar curve is an ellipse if its image is a nondegenerate affine image of the unit
circle. This definition includes circles. -/
def IsEllipseBoundary (γ : ℝ → ℂ) : Prop :=
  ∃ c u v : ℂ, u.re * v.im - u.im * v.re ≠ 0 ∧
    Set.range γ = {z | ∃ θ : ℝ,
      z = c + (Real.cos θ : ℂ) * u + (Real.sin θ : ℂ) * v}

/--
**Birkhoff conjecture.** If a planar billiard table has a strictly convex boundary and its
billiard dynamics is integrable in a neighbourhood of the boundary of the phase cylinder, is the
boundary necessarily an ellipse (with circles included)?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 37 52]
theorem birkhoff : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ γ : ℝ → ℂ,
    IsStrictlyConvexBoundary γ → IsIntegrableBilliard γ → IsEllipseBoundary γ := by
  sorry

end Birkhoff

A table boundary is represented by a 1-periodic parametrization γ : ℝ → ℂ that is C², simple modulo integer shifts, and has everywhere positive signed curvature. This captures the requested smooth strictly convex closed boundary and fixes its positive orientation.

Phase coordinates are (s,d), where γ(s) is the current impact and γ(s+d) is the next impact. Restricting 0 < d < η < 1 gives a collar of one grazing boundary component; the reverse orientation supplies the time-reversed component.
The billiard reflection law is expressed by equality of tangential components of normalized incoming and outgoing chords at the impact point.
